problems.stem: A resume bullet reads: "Helped run the campus food pantry." Which rewrite turns the claim into evidence a recruiter can verify?
options: "Passionate, hard-working volunteer dedicated to helping others."
"Coordinated weekly intake for the campus food pantry, scheduling 12 volunteers and serving about 80 students per week across two semesters."
"Helped out a lot at the campus food pantry and learned so much."
problems.explanation: A verifiable claim names a concrete action, a number, and a scope. "Coordinated weekly intake, 12 volunteers, 80 students, two semesters" lets a reader check the scale and the role, unlike adjective-only or vague phrasing.

problems.stem: You worked on a class team that built a website, and you wrote the page copy. Which bullet states a defensible claim without overstating your role?
options: "Built and launched a five-page marketing website that increased traffic 300%."
"Single-handedly created the organization's entire web presence."
"Wrote and edited the copy for a five-page team website that launched on time for the spring campaign."
"Did website stuff for a class team project."
problems.explanation: Claiming credit for the whole site or a 300% gain you cannot trace is overstatement. Naming exactly your contribution (copy for five pages, launched on time) is both truthful and specific.

problems.stem: An AI tool suggests adding "Increased department sales by 25% through strategic initiatives" to your retail resume, but you only stocked shelves and ran a register. What is the right move?
options: Keep it; the AI knows what recruiters want to see.
Keep it but lower the number to 10% so it sounds more believable.
Reject it, replace it with a truthful bullet you can defend, and note in your AI-use log why you rejected it.
Keep it and add "as part of the team" so it is technically true.
problems.explanation: An AI suggestion is a proposal, not a fact. A claim you cannot defend in an interview is fabrication even if the percentage is softened. Reject it, write a truthful bullet, and record the rejection.

problems.stem: Which before-after pair is the stronger revision because it moves from a duty to an action plus a measurable result?
options: Before: "Responsible for social media." After: "Was in charge of all social media for the company."
Before: "Responsible for social media." After: "Scheduled and posted 4 Instagram posts per week, growing the account from 210 to 540 followers over a 10-week internship."
Before: "Responsible for social media." After: "Handled social media duties as assigned by my supervisor."
Before: "Responsible for social media." After: "Did social media and other marketing tasks."
problems.explanation: A strong revision moves from a vague responsibility to a specific action plus a measurable outcome (4 posts/week, 210 to 540 followers, 10 weeks). The other options just restate the duty in different words.
